column1: # OTD500 batch manifest — one row per device (used in the tool's Batch mode).
# You usually don't hand-edit this: switch the OTD500 Configurator to Batch mode
# and add/edit rows in the UI (it writes this file for you). This template is
# here so you can pre-seed a batch from a spreadsheet / RMS export if you prefer.
# In Batch mode the tool matches a plugged-in device to a row by its LAN MAC
# (read over ARP from 192.168.1.1
# label password (or the shared password if it's blank)
# `otd-<site_name>`. After login it verifies the device's real serial / IMEI /
# MAC against the row before writing anything.
# Only required column: site_name. Everything else is optional.
# Columns: mac
# - site_name:            REQUIRED. Device becomes otd-<site_name> (hostname + RMS name).
# - mac:                  LAN MAC as printed on the label / RMS export (case-insensitive;
#                         ':' / '-' / no separator all accepted
#                         20972775FEE6). Leave BLANK for a "planned" row — the tool fills it
#                         in (and the serial) the first time that device is configured.
# - label_password:       the unique factory password printed on the device. Leave blank if
#                         the device is already on the shared password (the tool falls back).
# - serial / imei:        used only to VERIFY the right device is plugged in.
# - esim_activation_code: optional LPA string (LPA:1$smdp.example.com$MATCHING-ID) to load an
#                         eSIM profile; leave blank to skip.
# This is the *.example.* template — copy it to manifest.csv (gitignored
# per-device passwords) to pre-seed a batch
column2: or just build the batch in the UI.
